'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Israeli–Palestinian conflict]], [[2021 Israel–Palestine crisis]]
**[[Israel Defense Forces|Israeli forces]] shoot Zakaria Hamayel, a 28-year-old [[Palestinians|Palestinian]] man during a protest near [[Nablus]]. [https://www.palestinechronicle.com/israeli-forces-shoot-kill-palestinian-youth-near-nablus/ (The Palestine Chronicle)] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/5/28/israeli-forces-kill-palestinian-in-occupied-west-bank-ministry (Al Jazeera)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[President of Turkey|Turkish President]] [[Recep Tayyip Erdoğan]] inaugurates the [[Taksim Mosque]] in [[Istanbul]]. Its construction was considered controversial as [[Taksim Square|its location]] was considered to be [[Secularity|secular]] space, with earlier plans to build it near [[Taksim Gezi Park|Gezi Park]] contributing to [[Gezi Park protests|protests in 2013]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-57290677 (BBC News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Delhi]], [[COVID-19 lockdown in India]]
*****The [[Government of Delhi|Government of the National Capital Territory of Delhi]] announces a "very, very slow" easing of its lockdown as the number of [[COVID-19]] cases decreases in major cities. Beginning Monday, construction work and operation of [[factory|factories]] will be resumed. [https://www.ctvnews.ca/health/coronavirus/delhi-announces-very-very-slow-easing-of-covid-19-lockdown-1.5446480 (CTV News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****[[Malaysia]] reports a record for the fourth consecutive day of 8,290 new cases of COVID-19, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 549,514. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/asia/covid-19-malaysia-sets-record-4th-straight-day-8290-cases-mco-14904190 (CNA)]
****In response to a record number of COVID-19 cases in Malaysia, the [[Prime Minister's Department (Malaysia)|Prime Minister's Office]] announces a two-week nationwide "total [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]]" from June 1 to 14, which will ban all social and economic activities with the exception of essential economic and service sectors. [https://www.malaymail.com/amp/news/malaysia/2021/05/28/putrajaya-malaysia-to-enter-total-lockdown-from-june-1/1977800 (''Malay Mail'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]]
****[[Indonesia]] surpasses 50,000 deaths from COVID-19. [https://www.beritasatu.com/kesehatan/779717/update-covid19-kasus-meninggal-di-indonesia-tembus-50000 (Beritasatu)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****[[Japan]]ese [[Prime Minister of Japan|Prime Minister]] [[Yoshihide Suga]] announces the extension of the [[state of emergency]] in nine [[Prefectures of Japan|prefecture]]s for three weeks until June 20, the last day of emergency in [[Okinawa Prefecture]], as the number of COVID-19 cases continues to remain high. [https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2021/05/28/national/state-of-emergency-olympics/ (''The Japan Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Pakistan]]
****[[Pakistan]] reports its first case of the [[Lineage B.1.617]] variant, which was first discovered in [[India]]. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/1866556 (''Arab News'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Taiwan]]
****[[Taiwan]] reports a record 19 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 78. [https://www.taiwannews.com.tw/en/news/4211974 (Taiwan News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Hungary]]
****[[Hungary]] reports its first two cases of the [[Lineage B.1.617]] variant, which was first discovered in [[India]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-hungary-variant/hungary-detects-first-cases-of-indian-covid-19-variant-idUSKCN2D913U (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Kosovo]]
****[[Kosovo]] signs an agreement with [[Pfizer]] to buy 1.2 million doses of the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|Pfizer–BioNTech]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]], with the vaccine rollout expected to begin on June 15. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-kosovo-vaccine-idUSKCN2D92D5 (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Republic of Ireland]]
****[[Taoiseach]] [[Micheál Martin]] announces the further easing of the COVID-19 restrictions. Hotels in [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] can reopen from June 2, followed by cinemas, gyms, outdoor service at restaurants and pubs from June 7. Meanwhile, indoor services of two establishments will be reopened on July 5, and international travel will be resumed on July 17 through [[Immunity passport|EU Digital COVID Certificate]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-57280235.amp (BBC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in the United Kingdom]]
****The [[Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency]] approves the use of the single-dose [[Johnson & Johnson COVID-19 vaccine]], becoming the fourth [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] to be approved in the [[United Kingdom]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/may/28/johnson-johnson-single-shot-covid-vaccine-approved-for-use-in-uk (''The Guardian'')]
***[[European Union response to the COVID-19 pandemic]], [[COVID-19 vaccine]]
****The [[European Medicines Agency]] authorizes the usage of the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine]] for people aged 12 to 15 years old, becoming the first vaccine to be approved for children in the [[European Union]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20210528-eu-drug-regulator-approves-pfizer-vaccine-for-children-aged-12-15 (France 24)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
****[[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]] enters a seven-day circuit breaker [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] until June 3 at 11:59 p.m. [[Time in Australia|AEST]] in order to reduce the spread of [[COVID-19]] after the outbreak reaches 26 cases. During the lockdown, all public and private gatherings are banned, schools are closed, restaurants and cafés are only allowed to offer takeout or delivery services, and [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic|mask]]s must be worn outside homes. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2021-05-27/victoria-covid-cases-melbourne-outbreak-lockdown-restrictions/100169172 (ABC Australia)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Fiji]]
****[[Fiji]] reports a record 46 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the national total to 360. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/443608/covid-19-fiji-records-46-cases-highest-recorded-in-a-day (RNZ)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Germany–Namibia relations]]
**The [[Cabinet of Germany|Federal Government of Germany]] officially recognizes the country's perpetration of the [[Herero and Namaqua genocide]] during its [[German South West Africa|colonial rule]] of [[Namibia]]. [[Minister for Foreign Affairs (Germany)|German foreign minister]] [[Heiko Maas]] pledges [[Reparations for slavery|reparations]] worth [[Euro|€]]1.1 billion ([[United States dollar|US$]]1.34 billion) for the descendants of the [[Herero people|Herero]] and [[Nama people]] to be paid within 30 years. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20210528-germany-says-committed-genocide-in-namibia-during-colonial-rule (France 24)]
*[[Russia–European Union relations]], [[Belarus–European Union relations]]
**[[Russia]] denies entry to [[European Union|European]] airlines for a second consecutive day. [[Air France]] and [[Austrian Airlines]] flights were rejected by Russia's [[Federal Air Transport Agency]] amid the continuing fallout over [[Ryanair Flight 4978]] and the subsequent flight ban in [[Belarus]]ian airspace. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-57271949 (BBC News)]
*The [[United Nations Security Council]] approves a [[United Nations Security Council resolution|resolution]] drafted by the United States to extend the [[arms embargo]] imposed on [[South Sudan]] since 2018 until May 31, 2022, due to the increasing violence and repeated [[Human rights in South Sudan|human rights]] abuses in the country. [https://www.barrons.com/news/un-extends-south-sudan-arms-embargo-for-another-year-01622244013 (''Barron's'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Aftermath of the 2021 United States Capitol attack|Aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol]], [[January 6 commission]]
**[[Republican Party (United States)|Republicans]] in the [[United States Senate]] block a bill to form a [[January 6 commission|commission]] to investigate the [[2021 United States Capitol attack|storming]] of the [[United States Capitol]] as the bill failed to pass by a vote of 54–35, making it the first filibuster used in the [[117th United States Congress]]. However, [[Speaker of the United States House of Representatives|House Speaker]] [[Nancy Pelosi]] says that the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]] will still "proceed to find the truth". [https://www.forbes.com/sites/andrewsolender/2021/05/28/35-senate-republicans-block-jan-6-commission-in-first-filibuster-of-session/?sh=1af07a8b69b8 (Forbes)] [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-05-28/senate-republicans-block-bipartisan-probe-of-jan-6-capitol-riot (Bloomberg.com)]
*[[2021 Colombian protests]]
**[[President of Colombia|President]] [[Iván Duque Márquez]] deploys [[Military Forces of Colombia|military forces]] to [[Cali]] following the deaths of at least three people in the protests. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-politics/colombias-president-deploys-military-to-protesthit-city-ivan-duque-bucaramanga-colombia-b1856233.html (The Independent)]
* [[Kamloops Indian Residential School]]
**A mass grave containing the remains of 215 indigenous children is discovered on the site of the former residential school in [[British Columbia]], [[Canada]]. [https://www.theglobeandmail.com/canada/article-remains-of-215-children-found-at-former-residential-school-in-british/ (The Globe and Mail)]
**Archbishop [[J. Michael Miller]] of [[Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Vancouver|Vancouver]] said he was “filled with deep sadness” after learning of the discovery of the children's remains that were found buried on the [[Kamloops Indian Residential School|site]]. [https://cruxnow.com/church-in-the-americas/2021/06/canadian-catholic-leaders-express-sorrow-over-deaths-of-indigenous-children/ (CRUX)]
*The Ireland [[Health Service Executive]] confirms that private medical data for approximately 520 patients was published online after the recent [[Health Service Executive cyberattack|cyberattack]]. [https://www.irishtimes.com/news/crime-and-law/data-of-520-patients-published-online-hse-confirms-1.4578136 (The Irish Times)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2019–2021 Israeli political crisis]]
**[[Yamina]] leader [[Naftali Bennett]] and [[Yesh Atid]] leader [[Yair Lapid]] announces that they have agreed to form a coalition government, which would make Bennett the next [[Prime Minister of Israel]] until September 2023, and for Lapid to serve until November 2025. The agreement is expected to be announced by Bennett on Saturday night, and the government will be sworn-in on June 8. [https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/politics-and-diplomacy/lapid-i-dont-know-if-well-form-a-government-or-not-before-mandate-expires-669478 (''The Jerusalem Post'')] [https://www.timesofisrael.com/report-bennett-lapid-reach-agreement-on-forming-coalition-to-oust-netanyahu/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
*[[2021 Malian coup d'état]]
**The [[Mali]]an [[Constitution of Mali|constitutional court]] declares Colonel [[Assimi Goïta]] as the country's [[President of Mali|interim president]], following the arrest of President [[Bah Ndaw]] and [[Prime Minister of Mali|Prime Minister]] [[Moctar Ouane]] by the [[Malian Armed Forces|military]] on May 24. [https://www.thehindu.com/news/international/mali-constitutional-court-declares-colonel-goita-transitional-president/article34671889.ece (''The Hindu'')]
